questions.question: When RestoreCommittedLogs replays committed entries inside NewRaft, can the replay fail to make progress because the FSM batch channel is produced into before its only consumer is started?
questions.discriminator: Compare NewRaft return for replay sizes at and above the batch-capacity boundary, including a real cluster restart with and without a snapshot bounding the replay; a return in every case would refute the hypothesis.

latest_interpretation.rationale: Conclusion: violated. questions.question: Can VerifyLeader report success while the leader can reach fewer voters than its voter quorum, because acknowledgements from non-voter replication streams are counted toward that quorum?

knowledge.statement: NewRaft() calls restoreFromCommittedLogs() synchronously, which clamps the store's staged commit index to the last log index, sets the commit index and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs flushes a commitTuple batch to r.fsmMutateCh every MaxAppendEntries entries and once more for the remainder, and the only goroutine that reads fsmMutateCh (runFSM) is started after NewRaft returns.
knowledge.conditions: RestoreCommittedLogs=true and a LogStore implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; no snapshot restored at or above the staged commit index.

knowledge.statement: For the captured code, the startup replay can enqueue at most 128 batches because fsmMutateCh is created with capacity 128 and its send in processLogs selects only on that send and on r.shutdownCh; with DefaultConfig MaxAppendEntries=64 this allows at most 8192 committed entries beyond the last snapshot, so 8193 or more replayed entries have no enabled progress path (no consumer exists and shutdow [preview: 62 characters omitted; see full record]
knowledge.conditions: RestoreCommittedLogs=true, restart with staged commit index exceeding the last snapshot index by more than 128*MaxAppendEntries.

knowledge.statement: Automatic leadership transfer and explicit leadership transfer use different target checks: pickServer (used when no id is given) skips every server whose Suffrage is not Voter, while an explicit id is only looked up in leaderState.replState, which contains an entry for every configured server including non-voters, and a successful lookup proceeds to replicate and send TimeoutNow without consultin [preview: 24 characters omitted; see full record]

knowledge.statement: appendEntries raises the receiving term by first testing a.Term against r.getCurrentTerm() and later calling setCurrentTerm(a.Term), which writes the stable store and then the atomic term without comparing against the value it read, so the decision and the write are not a single atomic compare-and-set; the same function later deletes a conflicting log suffix from the first index whose term differs [preview: 37 characters omitted; see full record]
